ives-diary.author: George Cecil Ives
ives-diary.title: Diary (George Ives Papers, Harry Ransom Center, University of Texas at Austin)
ives-diary.note: Manuscript Collection ms-02138, eadid 00060; Series III. Diaries, 1886-1949, 122 volumes, open for research. Most volumes carry daily entries from 20 December 1886 to 16 November 1949 - **note the diaries end in November 1949, not 1950**, though Ives lived to 4 June 1950. The transcript here covers 21 and 23 November 1906 only (transcription by Brian Lewis, personal communication). Other diary passages must be quoted via the secondary work that prints them (Cook, Kaplan, Stokes, Lewis), cited at that work's page. **Cook's volume numbers are the Center's volume numbers** - his endnote 62 cites vol. 76 for 14 September 1920, and the container list gives v.76 as 2 September - 24 October 1920 - so every diary citation in Cook's endnotes (printed 125-131) converts directly into a requestable container. Bloodworth's 1909 arrival falls in v.51-55 (6 November 1907 - 14 June 1911); the 1939 will falls in v.104 (28 March 1939 - 18 March 1940) on either of Cook's two conflicting dates for it, October or 1 December 1939. Volumes 1-60 are bound in groups of five and 'bound very tightly and require special care when opening', which constrains reproduction. Ives indexed every volume from vol. 13 on, each index pointing to that volume's own page numbers - so the cheap way into an undated question is the index pages, not the volumes. Ives also wrote in several codes; see 'A Catalogue of the George Ives Collection', an appendix to the inventory. The address book (box 5, folder 8) 'provides cross references to his diaries'.

Several of the chapter's most quotable claims (the Goddard daughters' departure, Matilda Hayes, Charles French) rest on endnotes crediting Brian Lewis, personal communication, with no archival citation.

vivien-woman-appeared-1904.title: Une femme m'apparut…
vivien-woman-appeared-1904.note: The first edition, in French. BnF Partenariats EPUB (2016, ISBN 9782346053018) of the Gallica digitisation ark:/12148/bpt6k113413z, publisher given as A. glasgow-1997-your-john.title: Your John: The Love Letters of Radclyffe Hall
glasgow-1997-your-john.note: Radclyffe Hall's letters to Evguenia Souline, 1934-1942, ed. Joanne Glasgow (New York University Press, 1997). The scan is a 30-page extract - front matter and introduction plus printed pages to 80, against a volume ending at printed 271 - so no null finding from it may be stated as whole-volume. The scan is two printed pages per PDF page, with folios legible in the running heads; the text layer misreads words and reorders blocks, so transcription must be from the rendered page. Batten had been dead since 1916, and the only thing in the volume bearing on the Hall-Batten years is Glasgow's hedged footnote at printed 29 n. 1.

baker-1985-our-three-selves.author: Michael Baker
baker-1985-our-three-selves.title: Our Three Selves: The Life of Radclyffe Hall
baker-1985-our-three-selves.note: 422-pp text-layered PDF; printed folio = PDF page - 16, with folios in the running head.

troubridge-1961-life-and-death.author: Una Vincenzo, Lady Troubridge
troubridge-1961-life-and-death.title: The Life and Death of Radclyffe Hall

troubridge-1961-life-and-death.note: 192-pp text-layered PDF; printed folio = PDF page + 2 (an unusually negative offset). Troubridge calls Hall 'John' throughout. She was Mabel Batten's cousin, so her account of the Hall-Batten years (printed c. 40) is close-range testimony about a relationship she was not party to.

troubridge-diaries-hrc.author: Una Vincenzo, Lady Troubridge
troubridge-diaries-hrc.title: Diaries (Radclyffe Hall and Una Vincenzo, Lady Troubridge Collection, Harry Ransom Center)
troubridge-diaries-hrc.note: Unpublished; cite by entry date. Manuscript Collection ms-01793, eadid 00163. 131 volumes is the combined total across two series: Series II holds the 60-volume set running 27 December 1930 to 21 June 1943, containers 26.1-32.4; Series III holds 71 further volumes, 11 December 1943 to 21 January 1951, boxes 38-45 (formerly numbered 1-8). The two series are not interchangeable: the Series III volumes were written as letters to Hall after her death on 7 October 1943, so they evidence Troubridge's grief and the estate, not the partnership in life. Note also that the diaries begin only in December 1930, fifteen years into a partnership that started in 1915 - they cannot speak to its first half at all. Supplemented by daybooks for 1934, 1935, 1941 and 1942 (Container 33.1 onward). Condition: 'Some materials in Series I. and II. are extensively water damaged, suffering rust and mold.' Access: open, but researchers must create an online account. Same repository as the Ives diary. Vol. 1 (Container 26.1) opens the diary and states its purpose; Vol. 22, 14 June - 9 October 1934 (Container 28.3) covers the start of the Souline affair, Hall's letters to Souline beginning July 1934; Vol. 60, 6 February - 21 June 1943 (Container 32.4) is the last before Hall's death. Troubridge's own 68 letters to Souline, 1934-1942, are Container 50.5-6. The single most relevant document to this pair, described in the scope note but not itemised in the container list: a letter 'To the Executors of my Will', written by Troubridge February 1944 and revised September 1944, 'regarding the nature of Troubridge and Hall's relationship with Souline and instructions for the destruction of Troubridge's diaries'. Container 36.1 is the likeliest home; ask the Center to locate it.

claes-y90s-shannon-bio.author: Koenraad Claes
claes-y90s-shannon-bio.title: Charles Haslewood Shannon (1863-1937) (Y90s Biographies)
claes-y90s-shannon-bio.publisher: Yellow Nineties 2.0, ed. Lorraine Janzen Kooistra, Ryerson University Centre for Digital Humanities
claes-y90s-shannon-bio.note: Unpaginated - cite by paragraph, counting body paragraphs from the first and including the two block quotations. Https://1890s.ca/shannon_bio/. The fullest open-access account of the Ricketts-Shannon partnership; its evidence base is Delaney 1990 and Cook 2012. Contains one internal error: it dates Symonds's conviction that the two were 'an item' to the mid-Nineties, but Symonds died in 1893.

frankel-y90s-ricketts-bio.author: Nicholas Frankel
frankel-y90s-ricketts-bio.title: Charles de Sousy Ricketts (1866-1931) (Y90s Biographies)
frankel-y90s-ricketts-bio.publisher: Yellow Nineties 2.0, ed. Lorraine Janzen Kooistra, Ryerson University Centre for Digital Humanities
frankel-y90s-ricketts-bio.note: Unpaginated - cite by paragraph. Https://1890s.ca/ricketts_bio/. Copyright line reads 2010; the page's own mla citation gives the Y90s edition as 2019. Same author as frankel-2017.

ricketts-self-portrait-1939.author: Charles Ricketts
ricketts-self-portrait-1939.editors: T. Sturge Moore (compiler) and Cecil Lewis (editor)
ricketts-self-portrait-1939.title: Self-Portrait: Taken from the Letters & Journals of Charles Ricketts, R.A.
ricketts-self-portrait-1939.note: Available only as 486 per-leaf OCR text-layer files with no page images (New York Public Library copy; the bookplate survives on leaf 2); 163 of the 486 leaves mention Shannon. The front matter is Cecil Lewis's preface and T. Sturge Moore's introduction - their prose is not Ricketts's own voice; the journal proper begins near leaf 40. Each leaf carries its printed folio at the foot, but the leaf-to-folio offset is not constant (leaf 50 = p. 22, leaf 126 = p. 96, leaf 376 = p. 342, leaf 447 = p. 409). Because there are no page images, quotations are verified against a second digitisation, HathiTrust uc1.$b73973 (University of California copy of the same 1939 Peter Davies printing), whose search-only index confirms folios and readings and makes absence testable.

delaney-1990.author: J. G. P. Delaney
delaney-1990.title: Charles Ricketts: A Biography
delaney-1990.note: The standard life. 464-page PDF with a noisy OCR text layer (finding aid only); printed folio = PDF page - 28, with folios in the running head beside the chapter title. It is the source Cook 2014 cites for the quotations he takes from Ricketts's unpublished letters - including 'the forty years of perfect companionship I have enjoyed' (p. 389, Ricketts to John Gray, late 1929), which is not in Ricketts's Self-Portrait and survives nowhere else in print - and of the 'basically heterosexual' reading of Shannon that Cook argues with (Cook p. 34). Delaney's endnotes name recipients and give conjectural dates in square brackets; both are preserved here.

field-2009-thain-parejo.author: Katharine Bradley and Edith Cooper ('Michael Field')
field-2009-thain-parejo.editors: Marion Thain and Ana Parejo Vadillo
field-2009-thain-parejo.title: Michael Field, the Poet: Published and Manuscript Materials

Its introduction (p. 23 n. 3) also quotes Works and Days p. 16, independently corroborating that page number.

vancapelleveen-blog.author: Paul van Capelleveen
vancapelleveen-blog.title: Charles Ricketts & Charles Shannon (weekly blog)
vancapelleveen-blog.note: Https://charlesricketts.blogspot.com/ - weekly since 2012, 750+ posts, by a curator at the kb (National Library of the Netherlands) who is **co-editor, with John Aplin, of The Collected Letters of Charles Ricketts** (Brill, 3 vols, 2026). sutherland-1989.author: John Sutherland
sutherland-1989.title: The Stanford Companion to Victorian Fiction
sutherland-1989.note: Standard reference for minor and mid-list Victorian novelists (Stanford University Press, 1989, 696 pp., ISBN 0804715289). Cited here for Violet Hunt's birth year, where it matters that this is the very work Wikipedia gives as its source for a date it then contradicts.

geoffroy-gagel-vernon-lee-letters-vol3.author: Vernon Lee
geoffroy-gagel-vernon-lee-letters-vol3.title: Selected Letters of Vernon Lee, 1856-1935
geoffroy-gagel-vernon-lee-letters-vol3.editor: Sophie Geoffroy, contributing editor Amanda Gagel; translators Sophie Geoffroy and Crystal Hall
geoffroy-gagel-vernon-lee-letters-vol3.note: Volume III (1890-1896) of Lee's letters, 815 pp, text-layered (title page reads 'First published 2024'). Robinson married Darmesteter in 1888, so the break itself falls in volume II (1885-1889), not here; but this volume mentions Robinson on 64 pages and Anstruther-Thomson on 84, and may carry Lee looking back on it.

vivien-foster-1982.author: Renée Vivien
vivien-foster-1982.title: A Woman Appeared to Me
vivien-foster-1982.short_cite: Vivien, A Woman Appeared to Me, trans. Foster (1982)
vivien-foster-1982.note: 116 pp; the text layer is badly corrupt ('like' as 'Hke'), so transcription is from the rendered page. This is the first-edition text: the copyright page states 'French text printed by Alphonse Lemerre, Paris, 1904', and Dagmar is present throughout (39 occurrences) - so it translates the 1904 original, not the 1905 rewrite. Quotations from it are Foster's English, not Vivien's French. Gayle Rubin's introduction is a substantial piece of scholarship and identifies the roman-a-clef cast independently of Parker.

vivien-une-femme-1905-repo.author: Renée Vivien
vivien-une-femme-1905-repo.title: Une femme m'apparut…
vivien-une-femme-1905-repo.short_cite: Vivien, Une femme m'apparut… (1905 nouvelle édition)
vivien-une-femme-1905-repo.note: The 1905 rewrite, not the 1904 first edition - the title page reads 'Une Femme m'apparut / nouvelle Édition / Paris / Alphonse Lemerre, Éditeur / M dccccv' (a HardPress reprint of a Boston Public Library copy; the '1877' in the filename is Vivien's birth year). The cast confirms it: Lorély (165 occurrences) - the 1905 replacement for the 1904's Vally - and no Dagmar in any spelling. This printed copy runs to printed p. 168 and contains no Dagmar chapters; but the French Wikisource text labelled 1905 has Dagmar 32 times, in chapters xxxv-xxxviii, so either this copy is shorter than the text Wikisource transcribed or Wikisource's 1905 is conflated. What is established is that Dagmar is absent from this printed 1905 copy and present in the 1904 (see vivien-foster-1982).

vivien-wikisource-1905-epub.author: Renée Vivien
vivien-wikisource-1905-epub.title: Une femme m'apparut…
vivien-wikisource-1905-epub.note: Source given as fr.wikisource.org/wiki/Une_femme_m'apparut/1905. Not citeable until the discrepancy above is resolved: it carries Lorély (the 1905 name) and Dagmar together, which no printed copy we hold does. Recorded so the next person does not treat it as a clean 1905.

bucke-calamus-1897.author: Walt Whitman
bucke-calamus-1897.title: Calamus: A Series of Letters Written During the Years 1868-1880 by Walt Whitman to a Young Friend (Peter Doyle)
bucke-calamus-1897.note: Two things in one volume: Bucke's introduction, which contains a long verbatim interview with Peter Doyle (printed c. 21-34), and Whitman's letters to Doyle 1868-1880 - both participants' voices. Pagination: scan number = printed folio + 13. Bucke's title says 'a young friend'; the 1897 volume is discreet by design, and the discretion is itself evidence of what was being handled.

murray-wwa-doyle-encyclopedia.author: Martin G. Murray
murray-wwa-doyle-encyclopedia.editors: Matt Cohen, Ed Folsom and Kenneth M. Price (archive); Donald D. Kummings and J. R. LeMaster (encyclopedia)
murray-wwa-doyle-encyclopedia.title: 'Doyle, Peter (1843-1907)', in Walt Whitman: An Encyclopedia, on The Walt Whitman Archive
murray-wwa-doyle-encyclopedia.publisher: Garland Publishing / Center for Digital Research in the Humanities, University of Nebraska-Lincoln
murray-wwa-doyle-encyclopedia.note: Whitman Archive reference entry on Doyle (whitmanarchive.org/item/encyclopedia_entry3), by the author of the fullest published biography of him ('Pete the Great', Walt Whitman Quarterly Review 12, 1994). Based on a pre-print of the Garland encyclopedia, 'silently updated to reflect recent discoveries or to correct errors'; cite by the entry, not a page. Murray also supplies the lead on Harry Stafford.

whitman-archive-correspondence.author: Walt Whitman and his correspondents
whitman-archive-correspondence.editors: Matt Cohen, Ed Folsom and Kenneth M. Price (gen. eds.)
whitman-archive-correspondence.title: Correspondence, on The Walt Whitman Archive
whitman-archive-correspondence.publisher: Center for Digital Research in the Humanities, University of Nebraska-Lincoln
whitman-archive-correspondence.note: Open scholarly transcriptions of Whitman's letters, each with a stable item id - cite by that id (e.g. Loc.01251), not by a page. Transcribed from digital images or microfilm, with notes derived from Miller's six-volume Correspondence (New York University Press, 1961-1977). Non-standard spelling is preserved and flagged in the markup; the writer's spelling is kept here. Published under a Creative Commons licence.

kantrowitz-wwa-stafford-encyclopedia.author: Arnie Kantrowitz
kantrowitz-wwa-stafford-encyclopedia.editors: Matt Cohen, Ed Folsom and Kenneth M. Price (archive); Donald D. Kummings and J. R. LeMaster (encyclopedia)
kantrowitz-wwa-stafford-encyclopedia.title: 'Stafford, Harry Lamb [1858-1918]', in Walt Whitman: An Encyclopedia, on The Walt Whitman Archive
kantrowitz-wwa-stafford-encyclopedia.publisher: Garland Publishing / Center for Digital Research in the Humanities, University of Nebraska-Lincoln
kantrowitz-wwa-stafford-encyclopedia.note: Whitman Archive reference entry on Stafford (whitmanarchive.org/item/encyclopedia_entry55); cite by the entry. Carries a date conflict with the archive's own correspondent note: Kantrowitz gives Stafford's marriage to Eva Westcott as 1884, the correspondent note gives 1883 - unresolved; both recorded.

wikipedia-mabel-batten.author: Wikipedia contributors
wikipedia-mabel-batten.title: 'Mabel Batten', Wikipedia
wikipedia-mabel-batten.note: Wikipedia, 'Mabel Batten' - a tertiary source, used here only for marriage facts and only where the underlying footnote was inspected. The marriage sentence is footnoted to Emily Hamer, Britannia's Glory: A History of Twentieth Century Lesbians (Bloomsbury, 2016 edn.), p. 94.

wikipedia-lillie-langtry.author: Wikipedia contributors
wikipedia-lillie-langtry.title: 'Lillie Langtry', Wikipedia
wikipedia-lillie-langtry.note: Https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lillie_Langtry - a tertiary source, used here only for marriage facts and only where the underlying footnote was inspected. The article attributes this period principally to Jane Ridley, Bertie: A Life of Edward VII, and to Theo Aronson; the divorce and remarriage narrative is standard in Laura Beatty, Lillie Langtry: Manners, Masks and Morals (1999). None was read at source. **Conflicts with the Complete Letters editors** on her age at her first marriage - see edward-langtry--langtry.

wikipedia-richard-le-gallienne.author: Wikipedia contributors
wikipedia-richard-le-gallienne.title: 'Richard Le Gallienne', Wikipedia
wikipedia-richard-le-gallienne.note: Https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Le_Gallienne - a tertiary source, used here only for marriage facts and only where the underlying footnote was inspected. **the marriage sentences carry no inline citation.** Wikidata Q545544 is not an independent check: it holds one P26 claim (Julie le Gallienne) with zero references and nothing for the other two wives, so the two web sources are one source. The standard life - Whittington-Egan and Smerdon, The Quest of the Golden Boy (1960) - and Eva Le Gallienne's memoirs are the places to confirm all three, and neither is in the repo.

wikipedia-louis-wilkinson.author: Wikipedia contributors
wikipedia-louis-wilkinson.title: 'Louis Wilkinson', Wikipedia
wikipedia-louis-wilkinson.note: Https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Wilkinson - a tertiary source, used here only for marriage facts and only where the underlying footnote was inspected. Unusually well footnoted per marriage, which is why it is used here: Gregg to Bayley (1995) with J. J. Wilhelm, Ezra Pound in London and Paris 1908-1925 (1990), pp. 80-81, 102; the 1923 divorce to a T. S. Eliot letter of 9 February 1929; Ann Reid to Wilkinson's own Seven Friends (1953) dedication and to Friedman (2002), p. 13, with her 1932 death to Malcolm Elwin, The Life of Llewelyn Powys (1946), p. 207; Diana Bryn to Who Was Who; Joan Lamburn and the children to Wilkinson's Times obituary. Wikidata Q26435237 records only Gregg and is incomplete, not contradictory.

wikipedia-duclaux.author: Wikipedia contributors
wikipedia-duclaux.title: 'Agnes Mary Frances Duclaux', Wikipedia
wikipedia-duclaux.note: Https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnes_Mary_Frances_Duclaux - a tertiary source, used here only for marriage facts and only where the underlying footnote was inspected. **The paragraph carrying the Darmesteter marriage has a 'citation needed' tag dated August 2017**, so the year in it is not sourced on the page; the article's Blackwell footnote attaches to the preceding paragraph. Used here for the Duclaux marriage, whose year also conflicts with Wikidata (1902 against 1901, neither referenced).

wikipedia-una-troubridge.author: Wikipedia contributors
wikipedia-una-troubridge.title: 'Una Vincenzo, Lady Troubridge', Wikipedia
wikipedia-una-troubridge.note: Https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Una_Vincenzo,_Lady_Troubridge - a tertiary source, used here only for marriage facts and only where the underlying footnote was inspected. Corroborates the Ransom Center finding aid, which is the better authority and is what the edge leans on. Wikidata Q3549170 sharpens the wedding to 10 October 1908, but its two references are an online genealogy network and a library blog post, neither a register entry, so the day is not adopted.

whistler-correspondence-marillier.author: The Correspondence of James McNeill Whistler (University of Glasgow)
whistler-correspondence-marillier.editors: Margaret F. MacDonald, Patricia de Montfort and Nigel Thorp
whistler-correspondence-marillier.title: 'Marillier, Henry Currie', biographical entry in the Whistler Correspondence prosopography
whistler-correspondence-marillier.short_cite: Whistler Correspondence, biography of H. C. Marillier
whistler-correspondence-marillier.note: Https://www.whistler.arts.gla.ac.uk/correspondence/people/biog/?bid=Mari_HC. A scholarly edition's prosopography, which footnotes this entry to J. L. Nevinson, 'Henry Currie Marillier', DNB (1971; DNB Online, Oxford, 1997) - the ODNB entry 34876, paywalled. A tertiary digest; Nevinson's entry is the underlying authority. The entry gives the wife as 'Katherine Isabella Pattison' and her father as 'John Pattinson' in one sentence; the wobble is the source's and is not corrected here.

wikipedia-john-fothergill.author: Wikipedia contributors
wikipedia-john-fothergill.title: 'John Fothergill (innkeeper)', Wikipedia
wikipedia-john-fothergill.note: Https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fothergill_(innkeeper) - a tertiary source, used here only for marriage facts and only where the underlying footnote was inspected. Names Kate Kirby as his wife and co-manager of the Spread Eagle, and records that Fothergill credited her in his own An Innkeeper's Diary (1931). Does not mention the first wife or the first marriage at all - Sox is the only source for Doris Herring.

lewis-personal-communication.author: Brian Lewis
lewis-personal-communication.title: Personal communication
lewis-personal-communication.note: Unpublished. Cited in the form Cook himself uses for Lewis throughout Queer Domesticities (2014), whose endnotes credit several claims to Brian Lewis by personal communication with no archival citation. Lewis is Ives's biographer and has read the diaries directly.
